narrative.overview: Argus is a precision instrument with a non-reflective finish. One operator stares at it for hours, moving between attack-surface maps and threat-intel verdicts, so every surface is calm and matte: deep navy-charcoal and olive in the dark theme, warm beige and cream in the light one, with no glossy gradients, no colored glow, and no decoration competing with the data. Color is a scarce resource spent only on meaning — a single muted olive accent carries primary action and 'you are here', and a small set of earthen status hues appear only where they encode a finding, a metric, or a severity. Components are refined and restrained: thin borders, gentle radii, a faint neutral lift rather than a drop, and interactive states that shift tone by a single step instead of announcing themselves. This is an Operate surface, so scanability and consistency outrank expression; the craft shows in tabular numerals, monospace for every machine value, enforced contrast in both themes, and motion a reduced-motion preference fully disables.
keyCharacteristics: Matte, non-reflective surfaces in two first-class themes (dark default, warm light).
A single olive accent; color otherwise reserved for status and findings.
Thin lines, gentle radii (10px controls, 16px cards), quiet neutral shadows.
Inter for text, JetBrains Mono for every value; tabular numerals throughout.
Calm at rest; state changes are one tonal step, never a glow.

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Color encodes meaning — status, a finding, a data series — and nothing else. Chrome, containers, and layout stay neutral; a colored element is always answerable to 'what does this mean?'

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Olive is the only brand accent, and it carries primary action and current-location. Never introduce a second competing accent; reach for a neutral or a status hue instead.

rules.name: The Mono-for-Values Rule
rules.body: Any machine-generated value — IP, hash, domain, CVE, API token — is set in JetBrains Mono with tabular numerals. Human prose is never mono; values are never proportional.

rules.name: The Matte Rule
rules.body: No colored glow, ever. A selected or hovered element lifts with a neutral shadow and a one-step tonal change; it never emits light. shadow-glow is a quiet neutral lift, not an accent halo.

dos: Do route every color through src/index.css tokens (Tailwind names like bg-card, text-ink-muted, bg-accent); components never hard-code a hex.
Do read colors for SVG/chart fills through useToken() so they re-resolve on theme change.
Do set every machine value (IP, hash, domain, CVE, token) in font-mono with tabular numerals.
Do keep both themes correct and >=4.5:1 for text / >=3:1 for controls and chart marks when adding or changing a color.
Do convey depth with tonal layering and a hairline first; reach for a shadow only for cards, popovers, and the quiet selected lift.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion: the rise entrance and chart animations must fully stop.
donts: Don't add a colored glow, neon, or accent halo — shadow-glow is a quiet neutral lift by definition (The Matte Rule).
Don't introduce a second brand accent; olive alone carries primary action and current-location (The One Accent Rule).
Don't spend a status or data-viz hue on decoration; color must encode meaning (The Signal Rule).
Don't hard-code light- or dark-specific colors in a component; theme them through tokens so both modes stay correct.
Don't use sharp 0-radius corners or double borders; the form language is soft rectangles with single hairlines.
